finding: The product/CI correction supplies exactly PATHEXT=.EXE, but Windows PowerShell initializes its own process by appending .CPL. The first smoke incorrectly expected the inside-shell value to remain exactly .EXE.

primary_sources.finding: The legacy non-CORECLR initializer explicitly maps missing/empty PathEXT to .CPL and otherwise appends ;.CPL when absent.
The PowerShell maintainer identifies the same automatic .CPL addition as Windows PowerShell behavior that later Core had inadvertently removed.
The restored implementation uses the same explicit .CPL initialization rule.
